Blocks.Text: LinkedIn has released a new API endpoint, /jobRequisitions, to replace the older /simpleJobPostings API for job requisitions. This update helps keep job postings and job requisitions separate. Earlier, both were managed using the same API.

As RSC partners, you are required to migrate to the new /jobRequisitions endpoint by July 31, 2027. Go through the following sections to learn more about the endpoint updates and migration guidelines.
Note
The latest API version is 202604. Use this version in the LinkedIn-Version header for all API requests to access the most recent features and improvements.

Job posting: A job ad that is shown to candidates on LinkedIn or other websites.
Job requisition: An internal request used by recruiters or hiring managers to fill a job. It includes information like budget, job status, and approval details.
The following table summarizes the differences between job postings and job requisitions:
Jobs used for One Click Export (1CE) function more like internal job requisitions and are not meant to be seen by the public on LinkedIn or other websites. Separating the APIs will

To better serve RSC users' preference to manage sourcing at the Job Requisitions level and to 1CE candidates directly to requisitions.
To better capture this workflow intent and prepare for future integration enhancements.

To streamline LinkedIn's job posting APIs and align with how RSC partners manage sourcing, all RSC partners must migrate from the previous Job Posting API to the new Job Requisitions API. Posting RSC (private) jobs using Job Posting API will not be supported in the new versioned APIs. Use the versioned Job Requisition API instead.

Old requisitions (private jobs) using /simpleJobPostings will still show up in the 1CE dropdown.
New requisitions using /jobRequisitions will also show up in the 1CE dropdown.
When the new externalJobRequisitionId field value matches the old externalJobPostingId, only the Job Requisition will be shown and not the old Job Posting record. This keeps the requisition as one entry in the dropdown instead of creating duplicates.

ATS applications created with the old API will still appear in LinkedIn Recruiter.
New or updated ATS applications will also appear, as long as they are linked to a job requisition/old private job posting using externalJobRequisitionId.
The following table compares the fields in the old and new APIs, and highlights new fields introduced in the /jobRequisitions API.

Rows.Text: Unique identifier for the job requisition.
Current status of the job—either OPEN or CLOSED.
Marks the job as private (ACL-protected) or public.
Description of the job role and responsibilities.
One or more geographic job locations.
Nice-to-have skills in addition to basic skills.
Tags that describe the job function or domain.
Salary or wage details for the job.
Level of experience required (e.g., Internship, Senior).
Type of requisition—STANDARD or EVERGREEN. EVERGREEN must not include a parent requisition ID.
Total number of positions to be filled.
ID of the parent requisition for evergreen hiring model.
Time when the job was created in the partner system (epoch UTC).
Time when the job was last updated in the partner system (epoch UTC).
Preferred start date for candidates (epoch time, UTC).
Number of candidates hired for this requisition.

By July 31, 2027, ensure to

use the /jobRequisitions API to create or update all old and new job requisitions.
submit all new or updated ATS applications via the latest version of the atsApplications API, including the corresponding job requisition ID.
discontinue all traffic to unversioned atsApplications and simpleJobPostings endpoints for job requisitions.
Follow the guidelines below to use the appropriate endpoints for creating, updating, and syncing different jobs.

To create a new job requisition in RSC 1CE, use the /jobRequisitions endpoint to submit the job details.
To define the template stages that all job applications can progress through, send a stage update using the /jobRequisitionStage endpoint.

To update an existing job, use the /jobRequisitions endpoint to submit the revised job requisition details.
To specify the application stages for a job requisition, include the relevant stages via the /jobRequisitionStage endpoint when creating or updating the job requisition.

To create a new application, include the required atsJobRequisitionId field and post the related job using the /jobRequisitions endpoint (atsJobRequisitionId is mandatory for any new atsApplication record).
For detailed information on syncing ATS applications, refer to Sync Applications.

Jobs previously posted via /simpleJobPostings remain visible in RSC 1CE.
To update those jobs using /jobRequisitions, ensure the externalJobRequisitionId matches the old externalJobPostingId.

For job requisition (private) jobs syncing, use /jobRequisitions. For public job syncing, use versioned /simpleJobPostings endpoint.
Once you begin private job syncing via /jobRequisitions, do not use the old endpoint /simpleJobPostings for any private/internal job sync after migration.

Use the /exportedCandidate endpoint to retrieve exported candidates. For detailed information, see Retrieve Exported Candidates Overview. In the response, the values of the referenceEntityType field will be "REQUISITION" and the referenceEntityId will be the job requisition ID that was used to export the candidate.

To create a new ACL group, retrieve, update, or delete an existing ACL group, use /entityAcls with parameter entityType=JOB_REQUISITION.
To create, retrieve, update, or delete existing ACL assignees, use /entityAclAssignees.

Before scheduling your migration certification demo, complete every test case in Module 7 Certification. It covers migration readiness and cutover, job requisition and job requisition stage sync, ID parity and deduplication, application re-linkage, One Click Export continuity, ACL migration, and cross-cutting migration checks.
